Subject: Redwood Dedicated — follow-up after demo

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo today — the team found the Dedicated offering compelling. Per our internal kickoff, I wanted to capture our current sizing/requirements so you can recommend a starting configuration and any gotchas for deployment. Attached is a short spreadsheet with our initial traffic patterns.

High level:
- Primary use: text generation for conversational assistant + summary/QA pipelines.
- Steady-state TPS: ~30 TPS across all models (non-streaming + streaming mix).
- Burst: up to ~100 TPS sustained for short windows (5–10 minutes) during business hours.
- Concurrency target: 8 concurrent requests per model (we run two main model routes).
- Token mix: request tokens avg ~120, response tokens avg ~200 (total ~320 tokens per request).
- Model mix: 60% 13B family for lower-latency flows, 40% 70B family for high-quality responses.
- Security: VPC private deployment preferred; SOC2 evidence and KMS integration required.
- Timeline: pilot in August, prod by end of Q3 if procurement clears.

Questions for you:
1) For the 70B work, do you recommend H100 or A100 hosts in dedicate pools?
2) Given our burst profile, what is the recommended autoscale/burst strategy?
3) Any immediate cost-saving levers (quantized model variants, batching) you recommend for this mix?

Thanks — looping in Elena (infra lead) on the thread.

Cheers,
Samir Khan
Head of AI Platform
FintechCo

Hi Samir / Marissa — thanks for the details, that makes sizing straightforward. Below is a pragmatic starting proposal and rationale; happy to refine after any follow-up numbers.

Recommended baseline topology (pilot -> prod ramp):
1) Two-pool approach (separate capacity for 13B and 70B):
   - 13B pool (cost-optimized): 4x A100 (80GB) GPUs across 1–2 nodes. This pool handles the 60% traffic and meets the p95 < 700ms target with quantized 13B variants and batching.
   - 70B pool (quality-optimized): 4x H100 (80GB) GPUs on a single node to start. H100 recommended for better throughput on 70B FP16; we can run FP16 or bfloat-optimized kernels.

2) Autoscale & burst plan:
   - Baseline sized for steady-state (30 TPS).
   - Autoscale policy: add 1 node to each pool when CPU/GPU utilization > 65% sustained for 60s. For short bursts, enable pre-warmed burst nodes (cheap standby) so you can absorb up to ~100 TPS without cold-starts.
   - Consider a shared small burst pool (A100s) for sub-70B short spikes to avoid overprovisioning H100s.

3) Concurrency & batching knobs:
   - Concurrency per model route: start with 8 (as requested). We recommend adaptive concurrency + continuous batching to maximize throughput while keeping p95 latency goals.
   - Token handling: enable prefix KV cache for common prompts and response caching for high-repeat queries to lower cost.

4) Cost-saving levers:
   - Use quantized 13B variants where quality tolerates it (x2–3x throughput improvements).
   - Evaluate smaller sequence-length optimizations and aggressive batching for non-streaming requests.

5) Security & deployment:
   - Private VPC deployment supported; we’ll integrate with your KMS and provide SOC2 artifacts.
   - We’ll supply an onboarding checklist for network/firewall, DNS, and IAM.

Next steps:
- I’ll put together a short proposal (redwood_dedicated_proposal_v1.pdf) with estimated node counts and a cost range for pilot vs prod by EOD Monday.
- Marissa: can you confirm whether we should price with H100-only or mixed pools (H100 for 70B, A100 for 13B) in the first cut?
- Samir/Elena: Rafael will need a couple of sample payloads (one typical, one heavy) to run a quick micro-benchmark; can you drop them in the HubSpot deal link?

Happy to jump on a quick call to run through the math if useful.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
